name: flat-receipts
description: The control arm for the flat island's ONE remaining gradient. Shipped, a tile pays 6 to whoever gets there first and 3 to whoever is second, which is the whole reason to hurry now that the level gate, the ascending 4/8/16 and the fill-order bonus strip have all gone. This arm pays 5 and 4 instead: the same 9 VP per tile, the same island total, the same everything else - only the slope flattened. Read the shipped rule as the delta against it. What it is looking for is whether the race is real: if barn-at-game-end, game length and the delivery rate are identical between the two arms, then 6/3 is a number on a tile that nobody plays around, and the honest report is that the island has no time gradient the bots can act on. Note the standing warning from 2026-08-08: the bots take a delivery at a 97.9% rate whenever one is available, so they cannot dawdle and therefore cannot be paid to hurry. A null result here is EXPECTED and is not evidence against the rule - the instrument that can answer it is a table of humans. What a null result does rule out is any claim that 6/3 changes bot behaviour. ⛔ PASSENGERS PINNED 12/09/2026: Dean's plain-action balloon and Village Store ruling moved sixteen shipped leaves at once. This overlay predates that flip and every report taken against it does too, so each of those leaves is pinned here BY NAME at its PRE-FLIP value. Without it an arm read as a delta against a pre-flip base would silently gain a one-card flight, an always-present Aerodrome and a live coin economy. That is the 05/09/2026 passenger lesson: an overlay that should not move with the shipped default has to pin every knob the flip moved.
